Let
\[
h(z)=1+z^2+z^4+z^8+z^{14}\in \mathbb F_2[z].
\]
Define
\[
\delta=\deg\gcd(z^a-1,h(z)).
\]
Since \(21\mid a\), this is explicitly
\[
\delta=
\begin{cases}
5,& a/21\text{ odd},\\
10,& a/21\equiv 2\pmod 4,\\
14,& 4\mid a/21,
\end{cases}
\qquad
d=a-\delta.
\]

Then
\[
\boxed{
P_{R^a/Rg}^{R}(t)
=
a+
\frac{(1+t)(1-t)^d-1+dt}
{(1-t)^a+(1-t)^b+(1-t)^c-2+2t^2}
}
\]

Here is the derivation.

The entries of \(g\) lie in the \(x\)-socle layer of degree \(a-1\). If
\[
r=\alpha+\sum_{i=1}^a\lambda_i x_i+\text{terms of degree }\ge2\text{ or involving }u,v,
\]
then multiplication by \(g_i=X_i+X_{i+2}+X_{i+4}+X_{i+8}+X_{i+14}\) gives
\[
rg_i=\alpha g_i+
\bigl(\lambda_i+\lambda_{i+2}+\lambda_{i+4}+\lambda_{i+8}+\lambda_{i+14}\bigr)T,
\]
where
\[
T=x_1\cdots x_a=u_1\cdots u_b=v_1\cdots v_c.
\]
Thus \(\alpha=0\), and the only nontrivial linear condition is the circulant system with symbol \(h(z)\). Its kernel has dimension
\[
\delta=\deg\gcd(z^a-1,h(z)),
\]
so
\[
Rg\cong R/\operatorname{ann}(g)
\]
is a square-zero quotient with residue field plus \(d=a-\delta\) surviving linear \(x\)-directions.

Over the connected-sum algebra \(R\), the residue-field Poincare series is
\[
P_{\Bbbk}^R(t)
=
\frac1{(1-t)^a+(1-t)^b+(1-t)^c-2+2t^2}.
\]
For the square-zero quotient with \(d\) surviving directions, the relative factor is
\[
(1-t)^dP_{\Bbbk[y_1,\dots,y_d]/(y_i^2)/(y)^2}^{\Bbbk[y_1,\dots,y_d]/(y_i^2)}(t)
=
\frac{(1+t)(1-t)^d-1+dt}{t}.
\]
Hence
\[
P_{Rg}^R(t)=
\frac{(1+t)(1-t)^d-1+dt}
{t\bigl((1-t)^a+(1-t)^b+(1-t)^c-2+2t^2\bigr)}.
\]
Finally, since
\[
0\to Rg\to R^a\to R^a/Rg\to0
\]
is a minimal presentation,
\[
P_{R^a/Rg}^R(t)=a+tP_{Rg}^R(t),
\]
which gives the boxed formula.
